headline: Spring 2027 eighth-grade trip to San Juan, Puerto Rico approved; international travel and micro-mobility device policies advance to first reading.
summary: The meeting approved an eighth-grade trip to San Juan, Puerto Rico, for spring 2027. Two student policies, on school-sanctioned international travel and powered micro-mobility devices, moved forward for a first reading.
decisions: Approved sending the school-sanctioned international travel policy (JJHA) forward for a first reading, 8-0.
Approved sending the powered micro-mobility device policy (JLIDA) forward for a first reading, 7-0 with one abstention.
Approved the spring 2027 eighth-grade trip to San Juan, Puerto Rico, 8-0.
discussion: Micro-mobility device policy: Members raised safety and discipline concerns and asked how the police would handle a similar rule. One speaker said scooters help some students who must walk to school, and asked whether exceptions could be made.
MCAS on paper: Members asked whether the state would allow MCAS to be taken on paper instead of on computer, citing concerns that computer scores do not reflect student writing.

Puerto Rico trip costs: Members asked how students could practice Spanish on the trip and how costs could be lowered. Leaders listed a total cost of 2,568 and described fundraising and scholarship options.

Electric bus lettering: Members asked about the placement and cost of the lettering. The superintendent said it would cost a few hundred dollars per bus, and members said it would be paid from the transportation revolving account.
Elementary MCAS results: Principals reported higher numbers of students exceeding expectations and fewer not meeting them. They also discussed how Wit & Wisdom affects student writing.
